title: Finite words and their actual scalar and site comparisons
statement: Use the direct-image and open-extension data and arrows [def-pur-compact-scalar-site-diagram], [def-pur-normalized-inverse-image-square] between constant-coefficient vertices [def-pur-constant-coefficient-topos-model]. A word is a finite parenthesized expression generated by the identity at a vertex, a direct-image letter with its normalized inverse square and both direct models, an open-extension letter with its Cartesian open square, and composable concatenation. Its value records the four functors H_A,H_B,Htilde_A,Htilde_B, the scalar maps c_H,ctilde_H and site maps C_{H,A},C_{H,B}. Identity comparisons are unitors; direct letters use chi,d; open letters use beta,e; concatenation uses whiskering and canonical associators to paste these comparisons. At inputs M_A,M_B, SiteInvertibleAt requires d invertible at precisely the inputs of direct letters, recursively evaluating the prefix on each input; it adds no condition for identities or opens. A comparison of two values is four actual natural transformations theta_A,theta_B,thetatilde_A,thetatilde_B. Define SiteAt by the two equations C_{H',R} N_Y(theta_R)=thetatilde_R N_X C_{H,R} at M_R; ScalarAt by c_{H'} S_Y(theta_A)=theta_B S_X c_H at M_A; TildeScalarAt by the same scalar equation on an arbitrary tilde input. Define MixedAt by Htilde_B(delta_X) ctilde_H S_Ytilde(C_{H,A})=C_{H,B} N_{Y,B}(c_H) delta_Y. Here delta is the inverse of the vertex's specified lambda.
